books.section: C. President George Bush and the Persian Gulf War
The Presidency of George H. W. Bush

stem: Which of the following best explains why the United States went to war in the Persian Gulf in 1990-1991?

options.text: Iraq had attacked the United States mainland
options.misconception: Iraq never attacked the United States mainland.

options.text: The Soviet Union had invaded Saudi Arabia
options.misconception: The Soviet Union invaded no one in 1990; it was collapsing.

options.text: Kuwait had asked the United States to overthrow its own ruler
options.misconception: Kuwait asked for help against Iraq, not for the overthrow of its own ruler.

options.text: Iraq had invaded Kuwait and threatened the region's oil supplies

rationales.A: No attack on the American mainland happened. Background: the war was fought in the Persian Gulf, not at home.
rationales.B: The Soviet Union was dissolving in 1990. Background: the invader of Kuwait was Iraq, under Saddam Hussein.
rationales.C: Kuwait's ruler asked for rescue, not overthrow. Background: Kuwait wanted its country back from Iraqi occupation.
rationales.D: Background: Saddam Hussein's Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990, seizing its oil fields and massing troops on Saudi Arabia's border. President Bush organized a coalition to drive Iraq out and protect the world's access to Middle Eastern oil.
rationales.general:
1. Start with the photograph: American soldiers marching through desert sand.
2. Ask what sent them there. Background: in August 1990 Iraq invaded Kuwait, a small oil-rich neighbor.
3. Background: Iraqi tanks then massed on Saudi Arabia's border, threatening the world's oil supply.
4. President Bush organized a coalition to drive Iraq out and protect that oil supply.
Remember: the Gulf War began with an invasion of Kuwait, not an attack on America.
